It is not Lebanon that is emerging as the weak link in the memorandum, but rather Israel.

Once again, Israel refuses to be bound by any regional ceasefire and wants to include clauses that allows it to turn the ceasefire into a Swiss cheese. Just as it has in Gaza and in Lebanon before, it wants to render the ceasefire void of any meaning.

So far, the Iranians are standing firm. Not just because it needs to defend its standing amongst the Axis and not appear as having betrayed them. 

But also

Told @esaagar and @krystalball that Trump's deal with Iran - if it is finalized - is a devastating strategic defeat for Israel. It has, among other things, exposed Israel’s inability to confront Iran without overwhelming American military backing.

I address Trump's pending deal with Iran and the meltdown of the warmongers in this piece. But while Israel's supporters openly attack Trump, Israeli officials may keep a lower profile given Israel's elections and Trump's ability to hurt them politically in Israel.

But make no mistake, if a deal is reached, it will be a major strategic defeat for Israel.

Europe has nothing left but the pretense of relevance.

Europe could have been so much more than this.

I welcome the progress towards an agreement between the US and Iran.

We need a deal that truly de-escalates the conflict, reopens the Strait of Hormuz and guarantees toll free full freedom of navigation.

Iran must not be allowed to develop a nuclear weapon.

It must also end its destabilising actions in the region, directly or through proxies, as well as

The regional role in the US-Iran deal is astounding. 
1) Many regional states actively helped reach a resolution.
2) Their support protects Trump from domestic criticisms and takes attention away from Israel's opposition.
3) The regional anchoring ensures greater durability.

.@AJEnglish asked me if Trump could have achieved the same outcome without war. What the war did, in my view, was that the US came to realize that war does not work and, as a result, the US needed a deal that ensured long-term peace. That's the impact of having tried war.
